paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The variation curve of k^⊤β for AlphaEdit and MEMIT as the number of edits increases, with GPT2-XL serving as the edited model. As the results of Llama3-8B are not suitable for display in a line chart, they are presented in Appendix <ref>.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the variation of the scalar product $ k^\top \beta $ for two editing methods, AlphaEdit and MEMIT, as the number of edits increases, using GPT2-XL as the base model. The x-axis represents the number of edits on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 3000 with tick marks at intervals of 500. The y-axis represents the value of $ k^\top \beta $, also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.002 to 0.012 with tick marks at intervals of 0.002. The red line with circular markers represents AlphaEdit, which starts at approximately 0.004 when the number of edits is 0 and decreases steadily to about 0.001 at 3000 edits. The light blue line with circular markers represents MEMIT, which begins at approximately 0.0045 at 0 edits and increases monotonically to approximately 0.0125 at 3000 edits. Both lines are connected by solid segments, and the background includes a grid for easier value estimation.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the variation of the metric $ k^\top \beta $ for two editing methods, AlphaEdit and MEMIT, as the number of edits increases, using GPT2-XL as the base model. The x-axis represents the number of edits, ranging from 0 to 3000 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 500. The y-axis represents the value of $ k^\top \beta $, ranging from 0.000 to 0.012 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 0.002. The red line with circular markers corresponds to AlphaEdit $ k^\top \beta $, which starts at approximately 0.004 at 0 edits and gradually decreases to around 0.001 at 3000 edits, remaining relatively flat after 1000 edits. The light blue line with circular markers corresponds to MEMIT $ k^\top \beta $, which starts at approximately 0.005 at 0 edits and steadily increases to about 0.012 at 3000 edits, showing a consistent upward trend throughout the range.
